source_location: main text p. 528 (PDF page 10), Fig. 6c, UTL1 adsorption, solid blue triangles
notes: archive: fig6c_UTL1_adsorption.json; isotherm_point_count counted on plot: ~40 solid + ~20 open markers (approximate, crowded low-pressure region and overlapping open markers); wt% is W2 (m(H2)/(m_sample+m(H2)), Section 2.3); QSDFT (N2 77 K, slit-pore kernel, adsorption branch): SQSDFT 2045 m2/g (<35 nm), S<0.7nm 1148, S0.7-2nm 853, S>2nm 44 m2/g; V<0.7nm 0.32, V0.7-2nm 0.46, V>2nm 0.13 cm3/g; total pore volume = VQSDFT (pores <35 nm); average pore diameter = d50 volume-weighted median, d50 (d25-d75) 0.86 (na-1.39) nm; BET range: 0.02-0.2 (P/P0), BET consistency criteria ISO 9277:2022; elemental analysis (mass%): C 89.1, O 5.0, N 1.0, H 2.5, S n.d., rest 2.3; XPS (mass%): C 83.1, O 13.5, N 2.7, Si 0.7; N and O are inherent biomass heteroatoms, not deliberately introduced; d002 (XRD) 0.38 nm
basis_evidence: The measured quantity in the adsorption experiments is the excess gravimetric uptake of hydrogen (nex), i.e., the ratio of the mass of adsorbed hydrogen (mH2) to the mass of the sample plus the mass of the adsorbed hydrogen (ms + mH2).
